                        (ContinuousMultilinearMap.hasOpNorm'.norm (iteratedFDeriv Real p.snd f v))))

theorems.name: real_inner_le_lp_mul_lq_tsum_of_nonneg
theorems.type_signature:
∀ {ι : Type u} {f g : ι → Real} {p q : Real},
  p.HolderConjugate q →
    (∀ (i : ι), Real.instLE.le 0 (f i)) →
      (∀ (i : ι), Real.instLE.le 0 (g i)) →
        (Summable fun i => instHPow.hPow (f i) p) →
          (Summable fun i => instHPow.hPow (g i) q) →
            And (Summable fun i => instHMul.hMul (f i) (g i))
              (Real.instLE.le (tsum fun i => instHMul.hMul (f i) (g i))
                (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow (tsum fun i => instHPow.hPow (f i) p) (instHDiv.hDiv 1 p))
                  (instHPow.hPow (tsum fun i => instHPow.hPow (g i) q) (instHDiv.hDiv 1 q))))
theorems.raw_signature:
∀ {ι : Type u} {f g : ι → Real} {p q : Real},
  p.HolderConjugate q →
    (∀ (i : ι), Real.instLE.le 0 (f i)) →
      (∀ (i : ι), Real.instLE.le 0 (g i)) →
        (Summable fun i => instHPow.hPow (f i) p) →
          (Summable fun i => instHPow.hPow (g i) q) →
            And (Summable fun i => instHMul.hMul (f i) (g i))
              (Real.instLE.le (tsum fun i => instHMul.hMul (f i) (g i))
                (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow (tsum fun i => instHPow.hPow (f i) p) (instHDiv.hDiv 1 p))

For an alternative version, convenient if the infinite sums are already expressed as `p`-th powers,
see `inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq_hasSum_of_nonneg`.

theorems.name: real_sum_range_sub_log_div_le
theorems.type_signature:
∀ {x : Real},
  Real.instLT.lt (abs x) 1 →
    ∀ (n : Nat),
      Real.instLE.le
        (abs
          (instHSub.hSub (instHMul.hMul (1 / 2) (Real.log (instHDiv.hDiv (instHAdd.hAdd 1 x) (instHSub.hSub 1 x))))
            ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =>
              instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow x (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 i) 1))
                (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 i.cast) 1))))
        (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow (abs x) (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 n) 1))
          (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHPow.hPow x 2)))
theorems.raw_signature:
∀ {x : Real},
  Real.instLT.lt (abs x) 1 →
    ∀ (n : Nat),
      Real.instLE.le
        (abs
          (instHSub.hSub (instHMul.hMul (1 / 2) (Real.log (instHDiv.hDiv (instHAdd.hAdd 1 x) (instHSub.hSub 1 x))))
            ((Finset.range n).sum fun i =>
              instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow x (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 i) 1))
                (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 i.cast) 1))))
        (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow (abs x) (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 n) 1))
          (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHPow.hPow x 2)))
theorems.doc_string:
A lemma estimating the difference between $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ and its
Taylor series at `0`, where the bound tends to `0`. This bound is particularly useful for explicit
estimates of logarithms.

Note that thanks to the geometric series, the derivative has a particularly simple form, and means
that it is more convenient to avoid Taylor's theorem for this proof.

  Real.instLT.lt 1 r →
    Real.instLT.lt 0 x₀ →

        (∀ (n : Nat),
            GE.ge n 1 →
              (∀ (z : Real), Set.instMembership.mem (Set.Ico x₀ (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow r n) x₀)) z → P z) →
                ∀ (z : Real),
                  Set.instMembership.mem
                      (Set.Ico (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow r n) x₀)
                        (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow r (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)) x₀))
                      z →
                    P z) →
          ∀ (x : Real), GE.ge x x₀ → P x
theorems.raw_signature:
∀ {P : Real → Prop} (x₀ r : Real),
  Real.instLT.lt 1 r →
    Real.instLT.lt 0 x₀ →
      (∀ (x : Real), Set.instMembership.mem (Set.Ico x₀ (instHMul.hMul r x₀)) x → P x) →
        (∀ (n : Nat),
            GE.ge n 1 →

theorems.doc_string:
The real logarithm function, equal to the inverse of the exponential for `x > 0`,
to `log |x|` for `x < 0`, and to `0` for `0`. We use this unconventional extension to
`(-∞, 0]` as it gives the formula `log (x * y) = log x + log y` for all nonzero `x` and `y`, and
the derivative of `log` is `1/x` away from `0`.

theorems.doc_string:
**Minkowski inequality**: the `L_p` seminorm of the infinite sum of two vectors is less than or
equal to the infinite sum of the `L_p`-seminorms of the summands, if these infinite sums both
exist. A version for `ℝ`-valued functions. For an alternative version, convenient if the infinite
sums are already expressed as `p`-th powers, see `Lp_add_le_hasSum_of_nonneg`.
